record.title: China’s labor-skills center issues a cross-sector digital-intelligence capability framework
record.summary: China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Vocational Skills Appraisal Center issued a General Digital Intelligence Capability Framework on Nov 3, 2026, announced in a Nov 9 notice. The center says it is intended as a reference for skills training and assessment, curricula, vocational-school teaching, public employment services and employer skill standards, for audiences including job seekers, students, workers, job changers and flexible workers. The notice says it has six domains and 22 units and responds to rapid AI and digital change. The linked framework contents were not retrieved, and no adoption or employment outcome is established.
organizations: China Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Vocational Skills Appraisal Center

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Vocational Skills Appraisal Center issued its General Digital Intelligence Capability Framework on Nov 3, 2026; the official notice was posted Nov 9.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The issuing center says the framework is intended as a reference for skills training and assessment, curriculum development, vocational-school digital literacy teaching, public employment services and employer/industry skill standards; it targets job seekers, students, workers, job changers, flexible workers and ordinary-role workers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The notice says the framework contains six capability domains and 22 units, responding to digital-intelligence work changes and rapid AI development.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice does not establish adoption, funded delivery, the framework’s detailed AI competencies, or employment and training outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The notice links the framework as a QR-code image; its six domains and 22 unit contents, especially AI-specific skills, were not retrieved.
The notice invites reference use but does not establish adoption in curricula, training, assessment or employment services, nor any measured effects.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted, a cross-sector capability framework covering worker training, assessment, curricula and public employment services could influence how China prepares workers for AI-related changes. The consequence is meaningful, but the notice is nonbinding reference guidance and no adoption, detailed competency content or outcome is established.
limitations: The issuing center asks recipients to use the framework as a reference; the notice does not make it a binding standard.
The actual framework contents were not retrieved, so its AI-specific competency coverage cannot yet be described.
Issuance and intended use do not demonstrate local adoption, funded training, assessment delivery or employment effects.
organizations: China Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Vocational Skills Appraisal Center

The center says it is intended as a reference for skills training and assessment, curricula, vocational-school teaching, public employment services and employer skill standards, for audiences including job seekers, students, workers, job changers and flexible workers. The notice says it has six domains and 22 units and responds to rapid AI and digital change. The linked framework contents were not retrieved, and no adoption or employment outcome is established.

technical.claimed_result: The official notice reports issuance of a six-domain, 22-unit general digital-intelligence capability framework as a reference for several workforce and skills systems.
technical.compute_or_cost: No funding or compute allocation is stated in the notice.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Chinese notice establishes the framework’s reported issuance date, issuer, intended audiences and reference uses.
technical.implementation_status: Issued as reference guidance; local adoption, delivery and outcomes were not established.
technical.mechanism: A cross-sector capability framework is intended to inform training, assessment, curricula, public employment services and employer/industry standards.
technical.novelty: A dated national-level framework announcement explicitly connects worker digital-intelligence capabilities to rapid AI change and names multiple workforce-system uses.
technical.regime: China; general digital-intelligence capabilities for job seekers, students, workers and ordinary-role workers.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to a policy issuance. The QR-linked framework contents were not retrieved.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice cites an existing 2024–2026 digital-skills action plan; whether this framework adds distinct AI competencies cannot be assessed until its contents are available.

brief.title: China’s labor-skills center issues a cross-sector digital-intelligence capability framework
brief.why_it_matters: A reference framework intended to reach multiple worker groups and influence training, assessment, curricula and public employment services could shape how skills systems respond to AI-driven work changes. Its practical significance depends on the inaccessible competency content and future adoption; the notice alone establishes neither implementation nor effects.
